# 1. Data from unstructured websites

## Load necessary libraries
```{python}
import pandas as pd
import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import re
from plotnine import *
```

## Scrape data
Read in HTML from URL using `requests` library.
```{python}
URL = "https://tastesbetterfromscratch.com/meal-plan-142/"
HEADERS = {"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64)"}

response = requests.get(URL, headers=HEADERS)
```

Use Beautiful Soup to parse into a tree.
```{python}
soup = BeautifulSoup(response.text, "html.parser")
```

Find all recipe blocks.
```{python}
recipes = soup.find_all("p", class_ = "has-text-align-left")
recipes
```

## Create columns of data frame
```{python}
rows = []
for i in soup.find_all("p", class_ = "has-text-align-left"):

    # day of week
    day_string = i.text
    day = "".join(re.findall(r"\w+(?=: )", day_string))

    # name of recipe
    name_tag = i.find("a")
    name = name_tag.text

    # link to recipe
    link_tag = i.find("a")
    link = link_tag.get("href")

    # price of recipe
    price = "".join(re.findall(r"\d+.\d{2}", day_string))

    # append the data
    rows.append({
        "Day of the Week": day,
        "Name of Recipe": name,
        "Link to Recipe": link,
        "Price of Recipe": price
    })

meals_data = pd.DataFrame(rows)
meals_data
```

# 3. Automate it
```{python}
#| output: false
# function that scrapes meal plan data
def get_weekly_plan(plan_num):
    URL = "https://tastesbetterfromscratch.com/meal-plan-{}/".format(plan_num)
    HEADERS = {"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64)"}

    response = requests.get(URL, headers=HEADERS)
    soup = BeautifulSoup(response.text, "html.parser")

    rows = []

    for i in soup.find_all("p", class_ = "has-text-align-left"):
        # day of week
        day_string = i.text
        day = "".join(re.findall(r"\w+(?=: )", day_string))

        # name of recipe
        name_tag = i.find("a")
        name = name_tag.text

        # link to recipe
        link_tag = i.find("a")
        link = link_tag.get("href")

        # price of recipe
        price = "".join(re.findall(r"\d+.\d{2}", day_string))

        # append the data
        rows.append({
            "Day of the Week": day,
            "Name of Recipe": name,
            "Link to Recipe": link,
            "Price of Recipe": price
        })

    meals_data = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    meals_data
    return meals_data

get_weekly_plan(202)

# function that searches tasty API for matching recipes
def match_recipe(search_name):
    url = "https://tasty.p.rapidapi.com/recipes/list"

    querystring = {"from":"0","size":"100","q":"{}".format(search_name)}

    headers = {
	    "x-rapidapi-key": "a638670f82msh50c4d1549283208p17344djsnc360496a27fd",
	    "x-rapidapi-host": "tasty.p.rapidapi.com"
    }

    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=querystring)

    tasty_recipes = pd.json_normalize(response.json(), "results")
    return tasty_recipes

# combine functions together
def get_mealplan_data(num):
    weekly_plan_data = get_weekly_plan(num)
    
    #loop through each recipe in weekly meal plan data and find tasty data
    rows = []
    for _, row in weekly_plan_data.iterrows():
        tasty_table = match_recipe(row["Name of Recipe"])
        if tasty_table is None or tasty_table.empty:
            tasty_table = pd.DataFrame({"Tasty Recipe": [pd.NA]})
        else:
            # rename for display; keep all other Tasty columns
            tasty_table = tasty_table.rename(columns={"name": "Tasty Recipe"})
        tasty_table.insert(0, "Price of Recipe", row["Price of Recipe"])
        tasty_table.insert(0, "Link to Recipe",  row["Link to Recipe"])
        tasty_table.insert(0, "Name of Recipe",  row["Name of Recipe"])
        tasty_table.insert(0, "Day of the Week",   row["Day of the Week"])
        rows.append(tasty_table)
    complete_table = pd.concat(rows, ignore_index = True)
    return complete_table

df = get_mealplan_data(202)
```

# 5. 
```{python}
#calculate nutrition as calories
df["Carbs"] = (df["nutrition.carbohydrates"]*4)
df["Fat"] = (df["nutrition.fat"]*9)
df["Fiber"] = (df["nutrition.fiber"]*2)
df["Protein"] = (df["nutrition.protein"]*4)
df["Sugar"] = (df["nutrition.sugar"]*4)

#summarize nutrition facts over all tasty recipes
summary = df[["Name of Recipe", "Veg", "Carbs", "Fat", "Fiber", "Protein", "Sugar"]].groupby(["Name of Recipe", "Veg"]).mean().reset_index().rename(columns={"Veg": "Vegetarian"})

recipe_order = ["Chicken Divan","Beef Noodle Soup","Stuffed Shells","Vegetarian Stuffed Peppers","Chicken Gyros"]
summary["Name of Recipe"] = pd.Categorical(
    summary["Name of Recipe"], categories=recipe_order)

long_summary = summary.melt(id_vars=["Name of Recipe", "Vegetarian"], var_name = "Nutrient", value_name = "Calories").dropna()

(ggplot(long_summary,
    aes(
        x = "Name of Recipe",
        y = "Calories",
        fill = "Nutrient"
    ))
    +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
    labs(title = "Nutrition Information Per Recipe") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(axis_text_x=element_text(rotation=45, ha='right')) +
    facet_wrap("Vegetarian")
)
```

Note: No recipes were found in the Tasty search for Chicken Divan, so this visualization starts at Tuesday's recipe: Beef Noodle Soup.
